## Highlights
### Fixed
- Chromium Spaces can open devices on your local network, such as routers, NAS drives and home servers, once you turn on Crest Helper under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network, now Crest's own setting rather than one shared with other apps. A page that can't reach a local address says how to allow it instead of reporting a refused connection. - In Chromium Spaces, an http:// address you type or open now stays on HTTP, including when you reload it, instead of being switched to HTTPS. Links on pages still try HTTPS first and fall back to HTTP when a site doesn't offer it. - Files downloaded over plain HTTP in Chromium Spaces are no longer blocked outright: Crest asks whether to keep them, as it does for other risky downloads. - When you type a site without http:// or https://, Crest tries HTTPS first and opens it over HTTP if HTTPS can't reach it. Local addresses, such as nas.lan:5000 or a device name with a port, open over HTTP right away, and an address you type with https:// never falls back.
---
Development builds contain the newest changes and may be less reliable than stable releases.

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Downloads follow the Automatic Downloads choice of the site you’re on, including files it serves from another address, such as GitHub release files. A blocked download’s message no longer appears twice. - Chromium pages use your default zoom when they open and keep your chosen zoom as you navigate. - Chromium is updated to 154.0.8037.57 with upstream security and compatibility fixes.
